summary: A/B measurement of B-cee5 prompt stopgap: agents deviate from scan mandates either way, and no mechanical read-evidence exists to detect it.
trigger: Post-DONE effect measurement for B-cee5: same story (B-4e16), same harness, old vs new scope-plan template as the only variable.
lesson: Old full-scan prompt: the agent silently disobeyed (read 1 of 111 decisions docs, no audit trail) yet asserted complete coverage — in production such deviation is invisible, so coverage claims under the old prompt were unverifiable; when agents DO obey, the 2.4MB corpus costs ~600k+ input tokens (the original exhaustion). New bounded contract produced equivalent review quality (same load-bearing gaps and same spec-contradiction OQ) at 74.8k vs 79.3k tokens with a recorded enumeration + candidate basis + explicit non-escalation reason. Core gap remaining: what a reviewer actually READ is self-reported prose, not evidence — there is no read manifest bound to scope_check_save/review_pass_set and no transcript-derived read log, so future before/after comparisons and compliance proofs (detecting unrecorded full scans) have no ground truth. Prompt-layer stopgap is instructional only; proof needs mechanical read evidence.
reusePrompt: reviewer read evidence, scan compliance, token stopgap measurement, read manifest, scanEscalationReason audit, B-cee5 effect

summary: Parallel reviewers' destructive dist bite-tests on a shared story worktree race each other; serialize them or use an isolated worktree copy.
trigger: Two hosts/lanes both patch packages/main/dist/core/*.js in place to prove a smoke bites while other reviewers run smokes concurrently.
lesson: Destructive compiled-dist experiments (remove a registry name, run smoke, restore) must not overlap other reviewers using the same dist: a concurrently patched dist yields spurious FAIL observations. Either serialize the destructive step after all read-only lanes finish, or do what the round-2 quality lane did: build a scratch git worktree copy and bite there. Byte-restore and re-run the smoke afterward to prove the shared dist is intact.

summary: Run quorum_submit during REVIEW, before advancing to TEST, once all active lanes have current-round passes.
trigger: done_prepare doneClosure BLOCKED with review_assurance_floor_high_risk_3x2_or_fallback_missing, or quorum_submit refuses with missing current pass lane(s).
lesson: quorum_submit satisfies the 3x2 review-assurance floor by converting CURRENT-round signed review passes from ALL active reviewer lanes into host verdict records (hostA=claude-cli hostB=codex-cli); it refuses to fabricate. review_run_start/review_pass_set are REVIEW-phase-only, so advancing to TEST first (the round-2+ gate needs only >=1 receipt) strands the other lanes without a write path and forces a TEST->DEV->REVIEW round-trip to mint fresh passes in a new round. Correct order: all lanes pass in current round -> quorum_submit -> story_advance TEST.
reusePrompt: review assurance floor blocked / quorum_submit missing current pass lanes / review_pass_set not available in TEST

summary: ProofStory DONE shrinkage detector is a regex over summary text; shrinkage-flavored wording about neighboring items falsely blocks DONE.
trigger: story_advance DONE fails with unconfirmed_single_outcome_shrinkage: DONE summary appears narrower than the original snapshot.
lesson: evaluateDoneIntentEquivalence (core/proofstory.ts ~1582) flags unconfirmed_single_outcome_shrinkage via a regex matching out of scope, follow-up, not covered, deferred, excluded, partial, narrower etc. in the DONE summary. Describing a NEIGHBORING issue as out of this story scope / spun off as a follow-up in summary limitations trips the gate even when the story delivered everything promised. Fix by rephrasing (the sibling item is a different artifact owned by its own task; this story delivered fully) via summary_set, not by recording a false scope_shrinkage_decision_set.
reusePrompt: unconfirmed_single_outcome_shrinkage / DONE summary appears narrower than original snapshot

summary: A story whose diff includes package.json turns every later main merge into related drift: quorum, delivery-check, and review passes all stale and force a full re-review round.
trigger: done_prepare doneClosure BLOCKED with stale delivery-check materialHash mismatch plus review_assurance floor local rounds 0/N right after merging main into a story branch.
lesson: storyFilesHash covers the story diff file set. package.json is in that set whenever the story wires npm scripts (or gets scope-acknowledged version bumps), and DONE auto-bumps touch package.json on every merge to main — so any sibling story landing first changes YOUR story-owned material. Cost in B-3b05: one extra TEST->DEV->REVIEW round (4 reviewer lanes re-pass), fresh quorum_submit, fresh delivery_check_set. Mitigations: close stories promptly once quorum is bound; expect and budget the round-4 re-review when parallel stories share package.json; command-backed evidence must be actually re-run (refresh_stale refuses to rebind it silently).
reusePrompt: stale delivery-check materialHash mismatch after merge / review assurance floor local rounds 0 after mergeMain / related drift package.json

summary: Byte-budget assertions over output containing live machine state are nondeterministic; disable environment-dependent sections in fixtures via their documented env switches.
trigger: A previously green byte-budget smoke (brief-output doctor under 20000 bytes) fails minutes later with a bigger byte count and no code change.
lesson: The doctor brief includes the advisory host burn scan which streams the operator live ~/.claude/projects and ~/.codex/sessions state, so the smoke byte count varied with session activity (B-fa65 F-004: 20239 then 20606 on identical code). Fix pattern: the fixture invocations set LATTICE_BURN_ALERT_RECENT_HOURS=0 (the scan documented disable switch) on every doctor call so the budget asserts the projection deterministically; the budget value itself stays untouched. Generalization: grep the feature for an env disable switch before patching budgets or output.
reusePrompt: doctor brief under budget got NNNNN / brief-output-smoke nondeterministic / burn scan bytes vary

summary: A PINNED_EXECUTABLE_SOURCE_FINGERPRINTS repin is not single-source-of-truth even though it looks like one file.
trigger: B-3144: cli-engine.ts changed (new CLI wiring), requiring a repin in retired-authority-vocabulary-guard-smoke.ts's PINNED_EXECUTABLE_SOURCE_FINGERPRINTS map. That repin alone left validate failing with two unrelated-looking errors (red-evidence-target-binding-smoke.js, red-w2b-wiring-contract.mjs) because scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs independently lists every one of those same fingerprint values again, as a flat 'this literal must still appear in source' vocabulary check.
lesson: When repinning ANY structural/AST fingerprint (canonicalAstFingerprint or similar whole-file hash), grep the WHOLE repo for the OLD value before considering the repin done -- do not stop at the first file where you found it. At least two independent mechanisms (the guard's own approval map, and verify-process-fact-contract.mjs's vocabulary list) must both track the same value or validate fails with errors that give zero hint they are fingerprint-related.
reusePrompt: Before or after editing PINNED_EXECUTABLE_SOURCE_FINGERPRINTS in any *-guard-smoke.ts file, run: grep -rn '<old-fingerprint-value>' . to find every reference, not just the smoke file.

summary: effectiveEnvironmentDigest bakes in whatever ad-hoc env vars a command was run with, so a genuinely fresh PASS can still fail the next admissibility check.
trigger: B-3144: ran done_required_validate with LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS/LATTICE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS env-var overrides set (needed for an earlier, much longer 94-command validate step, not actually needed for this specific 2-command check whose default budget was already generous). Those extra env vars got hashed into the evidence's effectiveEnvironmentDigest (core/validation-evidence-reuse.ts effectiveValidationCommandEnvironment). story_advance --phase=DONE then recomputed the digest WITHOUT those vars and refused with effective-environment-digest-mismatch[0]/[1] -- this happened even on a second, genuinely fresh done_required_validate re-run, because I made the same env-var mistake twice before noticing.
lesson: Do not set ad-hoc env-var overrides (LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS, LATTICE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS, or any other ad-hoc export) on a done_required_validate/validate call unless that SPECIFIC command actually needs a longer budget than its own configured default. Extra env vars are not free -- they get baked into the admissibility digest and will mismatch the next consumer's recomputation, which does not see your shell's exported vars. Check the command's own default timeoutMs first (shown in validate's own progress output) before reaching for an env override.
reusePrompt: Seeing 'Cannot enter DONE: ... effective-environment-digest-mismatch' after a fresh-looking PASS? Check whether the producing command had extra LATTICE_*_TIMEOUT_MS or other env vars exported that the checking command does not have.

summary: A test fixture that 'poisons' state via a synthetic/fake identifier can be silently defused by an unrelated later fix that specifically targets fake or mismatched identifiers.
trigger: B-3144: injectPoisonedDuplicates/appendDuplicatesForRunId (in quorum-submit-smoke.ts) simulated the B-bf52 poisoning incident by tagging duplicate host_verdict rows with a synthetic non-current materialDigest string. B-f88e -- an unrelated, independently-landed sibling fix merged in via main the same day -- added a floor-side guard (eventsWithStoryFilesHashDowngrade liveIdentities skip) that specifically declines to downgrade a stale-material duplicate sharing identity with an already-native verdict. That guard silently neutralized the synthetic-drift fixture: the poisoning stopped reproducing and 3 regression checks (including 2 guarding real security findings F-024/F-025) started passing vacuously, with no test failure to signal it.
lesson: After landing ANY defense-in-depth fix (especially one that specifically detects/ignores fake, stale, or mismatched data), re-audit sibling test fixtures elsewhere in the codebase that simulate the SAME attack/incident class via a similarly-shaped fake identifier -- they may now be silently defused and passing vacuously. This is invisible from a green test run; it only surfaces by re-deriving what the fixture is supposed to prove and checking the fixture still forces that exact condition (e.g. temporarily reverting the new fix and confirming the fixture-under-test genuinely fails again).
reusePrompt: Landed a fix that makes the system correctly ignore/discount fake or stale data? Grep for other test fixtures constructing similarly-fake data to simulate the same incident class, and re-verify each still has real discriminating power.

summary: verification_evidence_add's per-intentRef command pin is permanently immutable, and custom intentRefs must still resolve to an authored PLAN-time verificationIntent -- there is no way to add or strengthen mechanical evidence for a checklist item once REVIEW finds a weak check.
trigger: A REVIEW-phase test-coverage reviewer found 3 verificationIntent entries whose pinned command+selector couldn't actually discriminate the scenario it claimed to test (e.g. a git-diff substring check that would also match a REMOVED line, so it can't tell 'preserved' from 'deleted').
lesson: verification_evidence_add refuses a second command for an already-evidenced intentRef with receipt-command-mismatch (the pin is immutable by design, anti-gaming). It also refuses a brand-new custom intentRef with intent_ref_unresolved unless that ref matches an intent already authored in checklist.json's verificationIntent arrays at PLAN time -- there is no command to append a NEW intent slot to an existing checklist item during REVIEW. When a reviewer finds a weak/non-discriminating pinned check post-hoc, the only real remedy is: (1) check whether a SIBLING intent on the same item already does the strong version of the same check (if so, cite it and resolve as sound-but-redundant); (2) if no sibling exists, independently re-verify the underlying claim by hand right now (a throwaway script/fixture) and record that manual re-verification plus the tooling gap explicitly in the finding_resolve reasoning -- do not try to force a mechanical re-pin, it will just error.
reusePrompt: verification_evidence_add receipt-command-mismatch / intent_ref_unresolved / weak evidence found during REVIEW / can't strengthen pinned checklist evidence / immutable intentRef pin

summary: A new lifecycle-gate artifact written OUTSIDE .lattice/story/actives/<storyId>/ needs its own runtime-artifact-registry entry (materialHash:'exclude') -- autoCommitStoryMetadata never reaches it, and auto-committing the write directly is the wrong fix (moves HEAD, breaks other signed evidence freshness).
trigger: B-a7c5 CHK-003's dev_memory_finish_decision writes to .lattice/dev-memory/finish-decisions/<storyId>.json, deliberately outside the story dir (it's shared dev-memory infrastructure, not per-story metadata). Left uncommitted after a write, this file fell through dirty-worktree classification to unexpected_dirty_files (blocking) and stranded review_run_start -- found live during REVIEW round 3.
lesson: First instinct was to auto-commit the write inside the handler (mirroring finding_resolve's commitHint/autoCommitStoryMetadata pattern) -- this worked for the immediate symptom but introduced a WORSE regression: the new commit moved HEAD, which retroactively invalidated any test-evidence.json/delivery-check.json already signed against the prior HEAD (stale_delivery_check materialHash mismatch), confirmed via a targeted repro before landing. The correct fix is almost always to register the path in core/runtime-artifact-registry.ts (RUNTIME_ARTIFACT_REGISTRY) with materialHash:'exclude', which routes dirty-worktree classification to the non-blocking runtime_artifact_changes category via findRuntimeArtifactEntry, AND ensures the path never perturbs currentMaterialHash in the first place -- no commit-timing/HEAD-movement side effects at all. Only add ignorePatterns if the artifact should ALSO be gitignored; a deliberately git-tracked-but-non-authoritative artifact (like this one) should have ignorePatterns:[] so it stays visible/shareable while still being non-blocking.
reusePrompt: review_run_start / dirty-worktree unexpected_dirty_files / new artifact outside story dir / stale_delivery_check materialHash mismatch after auto-commit / RUNTIME_ARTIFACT_REGISTRY materialHash exclude

summary: A materialHash-invariance test that only writeFileSync's (never commits) is non-discriminating: currentMaterialHash reads git ls-tree (committed state), so the assertion passes identically whether or not a runtime-artifact-registry exclusion actually exists.
trigger: B-a7c5's own F-005 regression test (added to prove a new registry exclusion works) only wrote the file, never committed it. A REVIEW quality-lane reviewer caught this in round 4 (F-006): deliberately removing the registry entry and re-running the test showed it still passed, because a bare write never touches HEAD/git ls-tree regardless of whether the exclusion exists.
lesson: When writing a regression test for a materialHash-exclusion fix, the test MUST actually commit the artifact (git add + git commit) and check currentMaterialHash across that commit -- not just before/after a bare write. A write-only invariance check only proves 'writing this file doesn't dirty an in-memory hash', which is trivially true for ANY uncommitted file regardless of registry configuration. Verify a new discriminating assertion's power directly: temporarily break the fix it's supposed to protect, confirm the test fails, then restore and confirm it passes again -- do not trust that an assertion is discriminating just because it currently passes.
reusePrompt: materialHash invariance test / runtime-artifact-registry regression test / currentMaterialHash write vs commit / non-discriminating assertion / verify test catches the bug

summary: lattice.config.json's validate.commands does NOT cover every test file in the repo -- the project's root npm test (full-suite-runner.js, driven by package.json's much longer test:serial-reference script list) is a broader, separate canonical test command that can catch regressions lattice validate and multiple REVIEW rounds all miss.
trigger: B-a7c5's CHK-001 change (a new gate check running before proofStoryDevGateFailure) broke packages/main/src/tasks/proofstory-intent-hardening-smoke.ts's DEV-admission assertions. 5 REVIEW rounds (4 lattice-review-quality passes + full lattice validate 96/96 green each time) never caught it, because that file is not registered in lattice.config.json's validate.commands. A round-5 quality reviewer caught it only by going beyond the two named fixes under review and running the project's root npm test as due diligence.
lesson: lattice validate (and by extension every REVIEW round that relies on it as its evidence) only exercises whatever is explicitly listed in lattice.config.json's validate.commands array. The project's root package.json 'test' script (full-suite-runner.js) runs a much longer, separately-maintained list that is NOT a subset check against validate.commands -- a file can exist in one list, the other, both, or neither. For any change touching a widely-shared code path (state-machine guards, core registries, shared handler utilities), run the project's root npm test at least once before DONE, not just lattice validate. Also: npm test's own HEAD-drift self-protection aborts the whole run if anything commits mid-run (e.g. a concurrent dev_memory_capture/finding_resolve auto-commit) -- run it with zero concurrent git-mutating commands, or its own protective abort looks like a mass test failure when it is not.
reusePrompt: npm test failing but lattice validate passed / REVIEW rounds missed a regression / validate.commands not comprehensive / full-suite-runner.js / full-suite identity drift HEAD changed during execution

summary: A test's generic top-level assertion failure message can mask the REAL underlying cause -- don't trust a surface error message as the root cause without tracing what actually happened first, especially when triaging a test as 'unrelated pre-existing' to justify not fixing it.
trigger: done-premerge-mainsha-recheck-smoke.ts failed with 'abort: external-advance shim fired (marker written) / the merge-tree interception marker was never created' -- I concluded this was an unrelated, pre-existing merge-tree-shim timing bug (confirmed the file wasn't in my diff, spawned a separate task to fix it). A round-6 quality reviewer added debug instrumentation and found the REAL cause: my own CHK-003 change (a new canFinishGuard check) was blocking the fixture's real story_advance DONE call with missing_dev_memory_finish_decision, BEFORE the story_advance call ever reached the merge-tree pre-check logic the fixture's assertion message was actually about. The fixture's assertion just checks 'did the expected marker get written', which is equally false whether the merge-tree logic never ran OR ran and failed differently -- the message doesn't distinguish those cases.
lesson: When a test fails with a message that sounds infrastructure/environment-related ('shim fired', 'marker never created', 'injection did not run'), and you're tempted to conclude 'unrelated, pre-existing, out of scope' -- verify by tracing the ACTUAL execution path (add temporary debug logging, or read the CLI's real stdout/stderr before the fixture's own assertion wrapper summarizes it), not just by checking 'is this file in my diff'. A file being untouched by your diff does NOT mean your diff didn't break it -- a new gate/check anywhere in the shared call path the file exercises can block it before it ever reaches the logic its own assertions describe. This is the same root-cause class as F-008 (a new gate running before pre-existing code the test expects to reach), just with a MORE misleading surface symptom this time.
reusePrompt: test failure message sounds like infrastructure/environment / tempted to call it unrelated pre-existing / spawn_task for a test failure / verify root cause before triaging as out of scope / shim fired marker never created
